summary: Midweek fractional GPU starvation triggers batched-route fallback oscillation for customer NimbleDocs
description: Issue summary: Customer NimbleDocs reports degraded throughput and repeated fallback routing during their midday traffic spike. Impact: sustained p50/p95 throughput drop on their dedicated pool, many short-lived batched requests degraded to fallback model variants; customer SLA degradation risk. Observed behavior: routing alternates between primary reserved-slot instances and fallback burst pool every ~90s; batch queue grows then drains in oscillation. First reported 2026-03-10 09:40 PDT. Customer reported increased 5xx rate when load is steady and many short streams are present.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NimbleDocs test workload (mix of long and short chatlets) on dedicated pool 'nd-reserved-usw2'.
2) Ramp sustained short 150-300 token requests from 200 RPS for 10 minutes while keeping background long streams at 25 RPS.
3) Observe routing logs and autoscaler events in the period 09:30-09:50 PDT; look for repeated attach/detach and fallback route events.
4) Check batcher queue length, GPU slot allocation, and KV-cache attach rates in metrics dashboard links below.
logs: [2026-03-10T09:39:12Z] api-gateway: 502 responses spike for /v1/generate -> request_id=8a3f..., upstream attach timeout=1.5s
[2026-03-10T09:40:05Z] autoscaler: evaluated pool nd-reserved-usw2: desired_slots=18 current_slots=14 reason=attach_backoff
[2026-03-10T09:40:07Z] serving-runtime: slot_attach_failed gpu=GPU-12 reason=IO_WAIT; evicting small-stream prefetch leases
investigation_notes: 09:45 - Initial hypothesis: autoscaler misclassifies short-stream flood as capacity shortage and repeatedly shrinks/expands. Evidence: correlated autoscaler shrink decisions with slot attach failures.
09:50 - Observed pattern: high churn of small batched requests causing KV-cache hotset churn; GPUs report intermittent IO wait leading to unsuccessful slot attachments for a subset of hosts.
10:05 - Compared to baseline (SUP-631210): similar noisy-tenant signature but this case has elevated short-stream fraction (~72%) leading to batcher serialization and eviction loops.
10:30 - Reproduced locally in staging by replaying NimbleDocs traffic profile -> confirmed batch queue oscillation when background long-lived streams co-locate on same GPU stripe.

10:50 - Temporary mitigation applied: increased small-request prefetch timeout and set conservative autoscaler cooldown for this customer's pool; observed immediate reduction in attach/detach frequency.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: combination of high short-stream fanout, KV-cache churn, and a latent driver-level IO wait on a subset of GPU hosts led autoscaler and router to oscillate between reserved pool and fallback tiers.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reported steady request rate but intermittent throughput drops starting 09:40 PDT. Logged their traffic sampler and asked for traces.
SRE (Liam): Investigating autoscaler logs; seeing frequent scale-down decisions triggered by failed attachments. Pulling GPU host S.M.A.R.T and dmesg logs.
Customer (NimbleDocs ops): We saw users hit higher latency and occasional 502s on 10-Mar 09:40-09:55 PDT. We can throttle short-chat traffic for experiment if useful.
SRE (Priya Rao): Noted two GPU hosts with elevated PCIe xfer latency (host-gpu-12 and host-gpu-17). Opening infra-priority alert for hardware triage (PR #918 referenced).
Support (Aisha): Applied recommended temporary routing change (hold fallback for 60s) and extended autoscaler cooldown. Monitoring with customer now.
Customer (NimbleDocs ops): After the change latency improved and p95 stabilized. Will report if recurrence happens during next peak.
SRE (Liam): Plan: replace suspected hosts from rotation after maintenance window; longer-term: refine autoscaler signals to consider short-stream fraction to avoid oscillation.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: increased autoscaler cooldown window for nd-reserved-usw2 and raised small-request prefetch timeout; held automatic fallback for 60s during client burst. Effect: immediate reduction in attach/detach events and p95 latency improved. Next steps: hardware triage for host-gpu-12 and host-gpu-17 (replace if IO wait persists), add autoscaler feature flag to weight short-stream fraction in decision, and schedule follow-up with customer for a controlled peak replay. Assigned follow-ups: infra (replace hosts) and runtime team (autoscaler tuning).
next_steps: 1) Infra to run diagnostic on host-gpu-12 and host-gpu-17 and schedule replacement if driver/firmware fixes do not reduce IO wait (owner: InfraOps).
2) Runtime team to add short-stream fraction metric to autoscaler decisioning and test in staging (owner: Serving Runtime).
3) Product Ops to coordinate a controlled NimbleDocs replay during off-peak on 2026-03-15 (owner: Solutions Engineering).
4) Update dedicated pool runbook to include a guidance section for noisy short-stream workloads and recommended autoscaler knob values (owner: SRE).
